title: How to Intrigue Everyone Without Saying a Word: You Only Have Ten Seconds to Show You're a Somebody
coreMove: Pause at the threshold and let your face, eyes, posture, and turn toward the person say present before your mouth says hello.
sourcePressure: Opening first-impression unit covering techniques 1 through 9: smile timing, sustained eye contact, visible attention, stillness, turning toward someone, greeting warmth, reduced fidgeting, situational reading, and room reading before acting.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is to tell readers to act confident or smile more. The useful version is timing and visible attention before speech.

hook: You never get a second chance at a first impression
counterintuition: People judge you by body language alone
Introverts just need to fake it
tryThisNow: Think of your best self before entering

exampleSpecs.domain: a museum conservator meeting a donor beside a newly unpacked textile crate
exampleSpecs.audience: a precise expert who can look cold when concentrating
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the donor trusts her with a fragile family heirloom before signing the loan form
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she stops reading the condition tag, turns her full torso away from the crate, lets her eyes settle on the donor, then lets a smile arrive slowly before saying his name
exampleSpecs.firstImage: blue nitrile gloves resting on the rim of a foam-lined textile crate

exampleSpecs.domain: a pediatric phlebotomy station where a new technician greets an anxious parent and child
exampleSpecs.audience: a medical technician whose hurry can look like indifference
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the child stays calm enough for one clean blood draw
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the technician sets the labeled vial down, stills both hands, lowers to the child eye line, and waits for the parent to see her smile before reaching for the tourniquet
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a lavender-top vial sitting in a plastic tray under fluorescent light

exampleSpecs.domain: a courthouse interpreter approaching a nervous witness before testimony
exampleSpecs.audience: an interpreter who must show neutrality and warmth without overstepping
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the witness believes the interpreter is safe enough to follow in court
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she closes the glossary folder, angles her chair toward the witness, gives a steady look, and chooses silence for two beats before explaining where she will stand
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated language badge clipped beside a folded court glossary

exampleSpecs.domain: a theater stage manager welcoming a guest conductor during sound check
exampleSpecs.audience: a backstage leader whose clipped efficiency can read as contempt
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the conductor feels respected enough to trust the crew during a tight rehearsal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before speaking into the headset, she removes one ear cup, faces him fully, lets the cue sheet drop to her side, and greets him as if the room can wait three seconds
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a headset cable looped over a clipboard full of cue marks

exampleSpecs.domain: an airport wheelchair attendant meeting a passenger at the jet bridge
exampleSpecs.audience: a service worker measured by speed but judged by first contact
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a passenger who hates needing help feels seen rather than processed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: contrast the first rushed approach with the second, where he locks the chair wheels, steps into the passenger sightline, waits for eye contact, and says her name before touching the handles
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folded boarding pass tucked under the wheelchair seat belt

exampleSpecs.domain: a competitive robotics pit where a rookie team captain greets an inspector
exampleSpecs.audience: a teen leader whose nerves make her fidget and over-explain
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the inspection starts with credibility or suspicion before qualification rounds
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she places the loose zip tie on the work mat, plants both feet, turns from the robot to the inspector, and waits until her hands stop moving before answering the first question
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a clear inspection sticker sheet beside a half-open battery case

skillTargets: choose first-contact visible signals in a scene where words have not started
distinguish warm smile timing from constant grinning
spot when fidgeting or half-turning undercuts a greeting
apply reading-the-room restraint before joining a live exchange

tryThisNowSpec: At your next doorway or call-start handoff today, stop your hands, turn your torso fully toward the person, find their eyes, then let your greeting arrive after that visible attention lands.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter
